Solution A is correct. Each equilateral triangle in the hexagon has two sides that are radii of the hexagon and one side that is a hexagon edge. Since the radii equal the side length, every triangle side equals a hexagon side. With a triangle perimeter of 21, each side is 7 inches, so the hexagon's perimeter is 6 × 7 = 42 inches.

Solution B's key step, "each triangle will have a side length equal to one-sixth of the hexagon's perimeter," is false. That would mean the triangle's side is 1/6 of the perimeter, but the triangle's side is one hexagon edge, which is 1/6 of the perimeter only if the perimeter is treated as the total length of all six edges, and that relation gives P_t = P_h/6 only when a triangle's perimeter equals one-sixth of the hexagon's perimeter. That is not the geometry here, since each triangle's perimeter is 3s and the hexagon's perimeter is 6s, so P_h = 2P_t = 42. Solution B's relation P_t = P_h/6 gives P_h = 126, which is wrong.

Final answers: A gives 42 (correct), B gives 126 (incorrect).

WINNER: A
